# Normal-preserving parity repair for a finite compatible fiber family

This synthesizes the ordinary conditional surface repair with the mixed
barycentric density-selection theorem. The support-roof argument below
is essential: the new coupling may reassign ordered base-pair masses,
and its midpoint is not presumed to remain on a target support face.
The proof enforces that requirement by one exact convex-order test.

Dependencies, in their stated scope, are:

* `candidate d7f1891e34b3ec5a`;
* its ordinary background bridge
  `candidate f38040720425d155`;
* `candidate 1bc960743a4bce34` and
  `candidate 93c94ac2c5c85584`;
* `candidate 5ea88513a25f2f4b`.

The first dependency's Sections 3-7 were independently audited in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
Its face-to-normal background is a separate dependency, not proved anew
here. No OC depth bound is asserted.

## 1. Data and theorem

Let d>=2, n>=0, and let P be a nonempty finite lattice-complete set:

    P=conv(P) intersect Z^n.

For z in P let K_z be positive compact convex bodies in R^d, compatible
under all convex combinations whose base lies in P. Let

    C=conv(union_(z in P) {z} times K_z).

Thus its sampled fibers are exactly K_z. Let eta_z be ordinary
(d-1)-dimensional surface measure on the normal bundle of K_z, using
the unique outward unit normal at surface-almost every point. Put

    eta=sum_z delta_z tensor eta_z.

Let gamma_-,gamma_+ be finite measures dominated by eta. Suppose an
old tuple coupling Xi_old of these measures preserves the normal n
between its two endpoints and has, almost everywhere, a midpoint

    (p,Y)=((z_-+z_+)/2,(X_-+X_+)/2)

with p in P and Y in the ACTUAL support face K_p(n). Retain n as an
additional coordinate of its midpoint law rho_old.

**Theorem.** There is another same-normal endpoint coupling Xi with
the same gamma_-,gamma_+, and with all its midpoints on the actual
target support graph, such that its midpoint law rho satisfies

    rho<=2^n eta.                                  (1)

At almost every normal, within EACH original endpoint parity class,
its new conditional physical midpoint law dominates the old one in
full physical convex order. Consequently these comparisons can be
integrated against any nonnegative bounded Borel normal weight.
The repair preserves both endpoint marginals separately for every
normal and parity class; it need not preserve individual ordered
base-pair masses or old conditional endpoint laws at a source mark.

If the old tuple law has a standard Borel source mark, the repair can
preserve that mark's joint distribution with normal and parity and
its conditional midpoint mean. Thus paired branches of a physical
martingale can be rebuilt without changing their source barycenters.

The uniform factor 2^n is sharp. A direct separate argument gives the
same statement for d=1, described in Section 8. No boundary measure
of dimension -1 is introduced for d=0.

## 2. One normal reference includes actual pair-average bodies

For every ordered base pair z,w in P, include the ordinary convex body

    M_zw=(K_z+K_w)/2.

Use the finite normal reference measure

    sigma=sum_z S_Kz + sum_(z,w) S_Mzw,

where S denotes ordinary surface-area measure. Repetition of a body
under distinct labels is harmless. Disintegrate the normal-bundle
surface measures of every labeled body against this SAME sigma:

    eta_D(dn,dX)=sigma(dn) mu_(D,n)(dX).

All conditional masses are bounded by one. Disintegrate the old tuple
law and the endpoint submeasures against sigma as well; their masses
are bounded by one because the tuple's normal marginal equals an
endpoint marginal dominated by eta.

The ordinary conditional surface theorem can use this enlarged reference.
To verify this, its original triple reference lambda is dominated by
sigma. At normals where both endpoint sigma-densities are positive,
t=d lambda/d sigma is positive, and each triple's conditional physical
measure against sigma is t times the one against lambda. The ball-mass
and pointwise density inequalities are homogeneous of degree one, so
they remain valid after this change. Where t=0 the endpoints have zero
conditional mass and no assertion is needed.

Apply that theorem to all the finitely many triples
(K_z,K_w,M_zw), where contact is automatic at every normal, and to
(K_z,K_w,K_p) whenever p=(z+w)/2 belongs to P, on its actual tight
normal set. Include the ordinary face-disintegration exceptional sets
for every labeled body. There is one sigma-full Borel set on which
all those conclusions hold simultaneously whenever the relevant
endpoint conditional laws are positive. Intersect also with the
full-measure sets on which the old conditional kernels have their
prescribed marginals, common parity, and actual support-midpoint
property. Work at a fixed normal in this set until Section 7.

## 3. Common intrinsic tangent dimension, without measurable coordinates

If two original conditional surface measures mu_(K_z,n) and mu_(K_w,n)
are positive, applying the ordinary theorem with target M_zw shows
that their exposed faces have the SAME affine dimension and the SAME
direction space. This conclusion does not require that their averaged
base be integer or that their pair be used by the old coupling.

Hence all positive original conditional surface faces at the fixed
normal have one common dimension m, 0<=m<=d-1, and one direction
space V of dimension m. Every relevant pair-average face has the
same dimension and direction. For m>0 the conditional surface laws
are equivalent to m-dimensional Euclidean measure on their relative
interior faces, with support equal to the closed face.

Choose orthogonal coordinates along V and V-perp. Write the affine
hull of the original face as b_z+V, with b_z in V-perp, and regard

    (z,b_z)

as a finite auxiliary base. The V coordinate is the continuous variable
of dimension m. This is an orthogonal decomposition of physical space,
not a lattice-preserving affine normalization claim. Mixed selection
allows arbitrary real finite auxiliary bases. All conditional laws
retain their original Euclidean measure normalization.

These coordinates need only be chosen for this one normal to prove
existence. No measurable choice of V, basis vectors, or density
representatives across normals will be assumed; Section 7 assembles
the final couplings directly in the fixed physical coordinates.

## 4. Temporary capacities at every auxiliary output level

Fix an endpoint parity class r with positive old pair mass. The old
integer midpoint condition makes the two endpoint submarginals in
this class have equal conditional mass. Let I_- and I_+ be their
positive-mass input bases. They share parity r. EVERY product base pair
z in I_-, w in I_+ has p=(z+w)/2 in P by lattice completeness.

The possible auxiliary output levels are the finitely many pairs

    t=(p,(b_z+b_w)/2).                              (2)

Their physical midpoint sets lie in K_p by compatibility. They need
not lie on K_p(n): there can be strict support surplus.

Assume first m>0. On marginal-full Borel differentiation sets choose
the finite positive density representatives f_z of mu_(K_z,n).
Intersect these endpoint good sets across the finitely many relevant
pair and target dependencies before choosing the representatives.
Set them to zero on the remaining points of their compact faces.
This changes no conditional input measure, and makes each representative
finite Borel everywhere. Each endpoint submarginal is dominated by its
corresponding f_z times Euclidean measure.

For each pair z,w use the target upper-density representative g_zw^+
of mu_(M_zw,n). The ordinary ball theorem gives, for EVERY pair of
endpoint points with positive chosen representatives,

    g_zw^+((X+Y)/2)
       >=H_m(f_z(X),f_w(Y)),
    H_m(a,b)=[(a^(-1/m)+b^(-1/m))/2]^(-m).          (3)

These representatives may be infinite on null sets, but their
integrals are the finite conditional surface masses. They supply an
integrable temporary ceiling at all levels (2), including off-support
levels: sum the finitely many g_zw^+ belonging to that same level.
Each summand uses the common m-dimensional Euclidean measure on that
level. No arbitrary pointwise essential bound is taken.

At a level (2) whose normal height equals h_Kp(n), every pair producing
that level is tight, since its height is [h_Kz(n)+h_Kw(n)]/2. The
ordinary theorem with target K_p then shows that mu_(K_p,n) is positive,
its face has dimension m and direction V, and its perpendicular offset
is precisely the offset in (2). In particular there cannot be two
distinct on-support auxiliary offsets above the same physical p.
At such a level REPLACE the temporary sum ceiling by the target
representative g_p^+ of mu_(K_p,n). The target version of (3) holds for
every producing pair, so this replacement preserves all needed
pointwise capacity inequalities.

We have now constructed one nonnegative Borel ceiling g on all possible
auxiliary output levels, finite as a measure, which dominates the
harmonic-power capacity of every positive endpoint tuple. The mixed
variable-density selection theorem gives a new coupling of these
class submarginals with law rho_r satisfying

    rho_old,r<=_cx rho_r,   rho_r<=g sigma_aux.      (4)

Here sigma_aux is counting measure on the finite distinct auxiliary
output levels, times ordinary m-dimensional Euclidean measure in V
on each level. Repeated base-pair descriptions of one level do not
create additional copies of that reference measure.

For m=0 the faces are points. Use their conditional atom masses as
the input ceilings. The ordinary ball inequality bounds the minimum
of the two endpoint atom masses by the appropriate pair-average or
tight target atom mass. The finite discrete version of selection
therefore gives (4), with the same temporary-level and target-level
choices. Its proof is the discrete inverse-endpoint argument: every
smooth strongly convex optimizer determines each endpoint from its
output, so the output atom is no larger than either reconstructed
endpoint atom; fixed-capacity compact separation then gives all convex
tests. No positive-dimensional formula is evaluated at m=0.

## 5. One finite convex roof test forces actual support contact

Write h_z=h_Kz(n). The concave support roof of the canonical hull over
conv P is

    h(z)=max {sum_a theta_a h_(z_a):
                    theta_a>=0, sum_a theta_a=1, sum_a theta_a z_a=z}.

Compatibility implies h(p)<=h_p at every p in P, while the single
input p gives the reverse inequality. Thus h(p)=h_p at every sampled
base, including boundary bases.

This roof has a GLOBALLY FINITE concave piecewise-affine extension.
Indeed the polyhedron

    conv{(z,h_z):z in P}+{(0,-s):s>=0}

in aff(P) times R is described by its finitely many facets. The
nonvertical upper facets have the form t<=ell_j(z). On conv P the
roof is min_j ell_j(z); vertical facets merely impose its projected
domain. Extend each ell_j affinely to the whole base space and set
h_tilde=min_j ell_j. This is finite and concave everywhere and agrees
with h on conv P. The construction also covers rank-zero P.

Consequently the physical function

    Phi(z,X)=n.X-h_tilde(z)                        (5)

is finite convex on the full physical space. It is nonpositive on C:
every canonical convex combination has height at most its support roof.
The old midpoint law is supported on actual K_p(n), so its integral
of Phi is zero. Every midpoint of the new coupling remains in C by
convexity, and has integer base p in P by the parity condition. Thus
convex order in (4) gives

    0=integral Phi d rho_old,r
       <=integral Phi d rho_r<=0.

It follows that Phi=0 rho_r-almost everywhere. All selected outputs
therefore lie on the ACTUAL support faces K_p(n). This argument does
not preserve or assume the old ordered base-pair assignments. It is
the reason they can safely change.

On those on-support levels, the ceiling in Section 4 was exactly the
target conditional surface measure. There is only one auxiliary offset
above each such p. Therefore (4) and (5) prove the physical bound

    rho_r<=sum_(p in P) delta_p tensor mu_(K_p,n).  (6)

All off-support temporary capacities have disappeared. Their only role
was to permit a valid unrestricted product-coupling optimization before
the roof contact was enforced.

## 6. Summing parity classes and refined support counts

Sum (6) over the at most 2^n classes. At this fixed normal this proves
the bound in (1). A smaller local ceiling is available: at base p,
count only classes r for which there are positive conditional input
bases z in I_-(r), w in I_+(r) with

    z+w=2p,    h_z+h_w=2h_p.                       (7)

No selected output from a different class can occur at p, because
every realized endpoint tuple has an allowed product base pair and
the roof identity forces tightness. Thus the density ceiling over
p is that finite count, at most 2^n. This is a maximum-preserving
coupling argument within each parity class and a SUM across classes.
No assertion removes overlaps of different classes at one target
fiber; the sharpness example below shows such overlaps are necessary.

## 7. Borel assembly and marked-source reconstruction

Return to the normal parameter. The old tuple measure disintegrates
into Borel finite kernels against sigma. Restricting by endpoint parity
gives Borel conditional input marginals and old midpoint laws, all of
mass at most one. The intended target conditional boundary measure

    eta_n=sum_z delta_z tensor mu_(K_z,n)

is also a Borel kernel of bounded mass on one fixed compact physical set.

For each parity r, consider the fixed-marginal coupling class satisfying

    rho_old,r,n<=_cx midpoint_*pi,
    midpoint_*pi<=eta_n.

Sections 2-5 prove its nonemptiness at almost every normal. These are
compact feasible sets defined by countably many continuous coupling,
convex-order, and domination constraints whose right sides are Borel
kernels. The audited measurable-selection construction therefore gives
a Borel choice directly in physical coordinates. Its constraints make
the target support graph automatic through domination by eta_n.
The nonmeasurable pointwise choices of tangent coordinates, roofs, and
temporary upper-density representatives are not being assembled.

Integrate the selected class couplings against sigma and sum the finite
classes. This yields one same-normal tuple law with the exact original
endpoint marginals, all actual support conditions, and rho<=2^n eta.
The conditional convex-order comparisons integrate with any prescribed
nonnegative Borel normal weight.

For source marks, select compact martingale kernels from rho_old,r,n
to rho_r,n by the same measurable assembly theorem. Retain the old
joint law of source mark, normal, parity, and old midpoint, pass through
that martingale, and disintegrate the selected new endpoint coupling
over its new midpoint. The final pair's mean is that midpoint. The
tower property preserves the old conditional midpoint mean given the
source mark, normal, and parity. Integration preserves the selected
endpoint marginals. This proves the marked assertion without fixing
the old marked endpoint kernels.

Every literal closed ambient halfspace still satisfies the pointwise
endpoint-midpoint implication for this one selected tuple law. No new
inequality for arbitrary supporting first-variation allocations follows
unless those allocations agree with the literal traces on the measures
being used.

## 8. Sharpness and the interval case

Take K_z=K for every z in [0,2]^n intersect Z^n, where K is any positive
d-dimensional convex body. Put gamma_- equal to the full boundary
measure on bases {0,1}^n and gamma_+ equal to the full boundary measure
on bases {1,2}^n. Pair complementary bases and identical boundary
points, retaining their ordinary normals. This is an old admissible
normal-preserving integer midpoint coupling.

Every admissible integer midpoint pair for these endpoint base sets has
base (1,...,1), regardless of its continuous pairing. Total input and
output mass is 2^n times the surface area of K, while the actual target
boundary measure at that one base has just one copy of that area.
Thus no universal ceiling smaller than 2^n is possible. The diagonal
continuous pairing attains equality.

For d=1 each normal is one of the two endpoint directions and every
support face is a point with unit counting surface measure. At a fixed
normal the auxiliary construction is purely discrete: endpoint atom
ceilings are the same after the common reference normalization, and
each actual pair-average interval has one endpoint atom of that value.
Apply the discrete capacity selection and the finite support-roof test
exactly as in Sections 4-5. There are only two normal parameters, so
assembly is immediate. The same product example proves sharpness.

The theorem repairs boundary transport with an exact sharp density
ceiling. It neither produces a deterministic OC point nor converts
convex order into source halfspace order. Those remain additional
requirements of the main proof search.
